text: Hardcoding a resource group name works for one environment, but the moment you need dev, staging, and production, hardcoding forces you to copy the whole file three times. A variable fixes that.

A variable block declares a type, a description, and an optional default. Inside a resource block, var dot name substitutes in the value. Override it at apply time, or more commonly with a separate tfvars file per environment.
An output is the reverse of a variable -- a value Terraform prints after apply finishes, so you or another tool can read a result without digging through the state file by hand.
The same configuration, applied with a different tfvars file, differs only in the values you intentionally changed. Outputs matter even more once configurations split into modules.
Variables parameterize input, outputs surface results. Next up: putting all of this together to provision a real storage account.
